span.label: method
span.quote: In this paper, we reformulate existing models into a single common framework we call Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs) and explore additional novel variations within this framework.

span.label: molecular property prediction from graphs
span.quote: To investigate the success of MPNNs on predicting chemical properties, we use the publicly available QM9 dataset (Ramakrishnan et al., 2014).

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We performed numerous experiments in order to find the best possible MPNN on this dataset as well as the proper input representation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: message passing on the molecular graph (atoms as nodes, bonds as edges): iteratively passing and aggregating messages between atoms
span.quote: a message passing algorithm and aggregation procedure to compute a function of their entire input graph

span.label: the models fit the DFT approximation, itself an approximation of true quantum properties
span.quote: the ability to fit the DFT approximation to within chemical accuracy would be an encouraging step

span.label: The towers variant improves scalability but is still insufficient for much larger graphs.
span.quote: The towers variation makes these models more scalable, but additional improvements will be needed to scale to much larger graphs.

span.label: Generalising to larger molecules is hard precisely when spatial information is used.
span.quote: Generalizing to larger molecule sizes seems particularly challenging when using spatial information.

span.label: Combining the towers variant with the edge-network message function did not work.
span.quote: Unfortunately, our attempts so far at combining the towers and edge network message function have failed to further improve performance, possibly because the combination makes training more difficult.

span.label: Some ablation experiments used a partial-charge input feature that would not be available in a real application.
span.quote: This feature is an output of the DFT calculation and thus could not be used in an applied setting.

span.label: Accuracy is measured against DFT approximations because experimentally true targets do not exist for the full dataset.
span.quote: The dataset containing the true targets on all 134k molecules does not currently exist.

span.label: The paper's headline term is redefined to mean error against its own labels rather than against nature, and it says so in one sentence.
span.quote: In the rest of this paper when we talk about chemical accuracy we generally mean with respect to our available ground truth labels

span.label: Two different error standards are in play and the paper orders them.
span.quote: For all 13 targets, achieving chemical accuracy is at least as hard as achieving DFT error

span.label: Eight existing models are re-described in the authors' own framework, with the derivations placed outside the paper.
span.quote: There are at least eight notable examples of models from the literature that we can describe using our Message Passing Neural Networks

span.label: graph neural networks / deep learning, applied to predict quantum-chemical properties of molecules
span.quote: using machine learning (and especially deep learning)

span.label: 'chemical accuracy' - TWO REFERENCE POINTS, AND THE PAPER PICKS THE NEARER ONE: the chemistry community's target error is relative to nature, DFT error is the gap between the simulation and nature, and this paper states that its own use of the phrase means error against its available labels - so the headline measures agreement with a simulation, not with a molecule
span.quote: The first is the estimated average error of the DFT approximation to nature, which we refer to as “DFT error.” The second, known as “chemical accuracy,” is a target error that has been established by the chemistry community

span.label: MPNN - A NAME GIVEN TO EIGHT EXISTING MODELS AFTER THE FACT: the framework is introduced as a reformulation of models already in the literature under one label, which is the inverse of the usual naming failure - here a paper renames its field rather than being renamed by it
span.quote: we reformulate existing models into a single common framework we call Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs) and explore additional novel variations within this framework

span.label: the prediction target - A MODEL OF A MODEL: what the network predicts is the outcome of a computationally expensive DFT calculation, so the object being learned is itself a simulation of the quantity of interest rather than the quantity
span.quote: A Message Passing Neural Network predicts quantum properties of an organic molecule by modeling a computationally expensive DFT calculation
